display.title: Hashem's Name: Rabbi Moshe Galanti and the Sheikh's Secret, Part 2
display.summary_short: A brachah is the payment Hashem accepts for our food. Rabbi Moshe Galanti finally learns the sheikh's secret, and it teaches him how to honor Hashem's name.
display.summary_long: Avraham ran a free inn in the desert and asked his guests to thank Hashem; whoever refused had to pay ten silver coins for a roll. A boy named Chaim buys a cupcake, and his father explains that since the whole world belongs to Hashem, eating without a brachah is like stealing from the Beis HaMikdash. At the bakery they learn that we pay farmers and bakers only for their work; the food itself is Hashem's, and the payment He accepts is a brachah said clearly, not mumbled. The story continues: the sheikh begs Rabbi Moshe Galanti to teach him the introduction to the seventh wisdom, and Rabbi Moshe agrees only in exchange for the secret of how the sheikh knows whether a sick person will live. After a two-day fast and immersions, the sheikh leads him through a hidden garden to a jeweled ark showing the words "Shivisi Hashem l'negdi tamid," with Hashem's name larger than the rest; when he prays, the name shines brightly or grows dim. Rabbi Moshe goes home and cries, asking whether he gives Hashem's name the same honor, and the storyteller reminds children to say every brachah with care.
display.lesson: Say every brachah clearly and carefully: it is how we receive our food from Hashem, and His name deserves the greatest respect.

advisories.note: The sheikh prays for sick people and foresees whether they will live or die.
